title: How do we make a number machine of our own?
description: A formula is chosen in the letter-numbers a and b, four number machines are written for it, and the rule is hidden for a classmate to find. A model formula is worked through.
teaching_notes: One idea: a formula of our own is written in a and b, and a classmate needs several pairs, not one, to find it. Watch for students who show only one pair of inputs and results.

source: Make a formula of your own with letter-numbers a and b, writ
video_script.why: A learner sees how to make a formula of their own, write machines for it, and why several pairs are shown.
video_script.substitution: the book's open task, worked through with the model formula three times a plus b
video_script.anchor: the open task of the book: a formula of our own in a and b, with four machines and a hidden rule
video_script.wrong_answer: one pair of inputs is enough
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says one pair of inputs is enough to show a classmate. Many rules fit one pair, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The model is three eigh plus b, which gives eleven, thirteen, seven and twenty four.

final_answer.spoken: the model formula three eigh plus b gives eleven, thirteen, seven and twenty four

maths_rules: model rule in words: three times the first number plus the second number; formula 3a + b
show only the inputs and results, and ask a classmate for the rule
Keeko test: the sum plus 4 also gives 11 for 2 and 5, but gives 9 for 4 and 1 where 3a + b gives 13
video_script.design: The open task stays on the board; one model formula is chosen in words, written with letter-numbers, put into four machines, and shown with its rule hidden.
open_questions: The task is open ended: any formula in a and b with four machines that fit it is right, and the formula three a plus b is only a model.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the letter-numbers a and b, four empty number machines, and a hidden rule for a classmate

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the letter-numbers a and b are written
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the hidden rule

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a task from your book. You make the formula yourself, with the letter-numbers eigh and b.
<bookmark mark='four'/>You write four number machines for it, and hide the rule from a classmate.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which formula could we choose, and how will a classmate find it?

beats.on_screen: the four empty machines stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: first input a, second input b; choose the rule in words first, then write it with a and b; the classmate sees only inputs and results

marks.names: the first input is labelled a and the second input is labelled b
marks.words: a rule in words becomes a formula in a and b
marks.hidden: the rule is covered, and only inputs and results show

narration: <bookmark mark='names'/>We call the first input eigh, and the second input b.
<bookmark mark='words'/>We choose the rule in words first, and then write it with eigh and b.
<bookmark mark='hidden'/>A classmate sees only the inputs and the results.

beats.on_screen: Given: the letter-numbers a and b; four machines to write; the rule to hide
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the letter-numbers eigh and b, and the task of four machines.

beats.on_screen: To find: a formula of our own, four machines for it, and the hidden rule

marks.find: the words formula, four machines and hidden rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to make a formula, write four machines for it, and hide the rule.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: rule in words: three times the first number, plus the second number; formula 3a + b

marks.words: the rule three times the first number plus the second number is written
marks.letters: the first number becomes a, the second becomes b, and 3a + b is written

narration: <bookmark mark='words'/>Step one, choose a rule in words: three times the first number, plus the second number.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>With eigh and b, the formula we choose is three eigh plus b.

marks.one: 3 × 2 + 5 = 6 + 5 = 11 is written in the first machine
marks.two: 3 × 4 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13 is written in the second machine

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, put two and five into the first machine. Three times two plus five is eleven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Put four and one into the second machine. Three times four plus one is thirteen.

marks.three: 3 × 0 + 7 = 7 is written in the third machine
marks.four: 3 × 6 + 6 = 18 + 6 = 24 is written in the fourth machine

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, put zero and seven into the third machine. Three times zero plus seven is seven.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Put six and six into the fourth machine. Three times six plus six is twenty four.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: show only the inputs and results: (2, 5) → 11;  (4, 1) → 13;  (0, 7) → 7;  (6, 6) → 24; the rule is hidden

marks.show: only the inputs and results stay on the machines
marks.hide: the rule 3a + b is covered with a card
marks.ask: the classmate is asked for the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='show'/>Step four, show only the inputs and the results, and cover the rule.
<bookmark mark='hide'/>Two and five give eleven, and four and one give thirteen. Zero and seven give seven, and six and six give twenty four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Then ask the classmate to find the rule.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Open ended. Model: 3a + b gives 11, 13, 7 and 24

marks.open: the words any formula that fits its machines appear beside the box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The model is three eigh plus b, which gives eleven, thirteen, seven and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Your own formula can be different, if its four machines fit it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the machines
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: one pair is enough, struck out; the sum plus 4 also gives 11 for (2, 5), but 9 for (4, 1) where 3a + b gives 13

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows one pair, (2, 5) giving 11
marks.test: the rule sum plus 4 also gives 11 for (2, 5)
marks.gap: for (4, 1), 9 from the sum plus 4 and 13 from 3a + b appear side by side
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and four pairs are shown

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one pair of inputs is enough to show a classmate. Two and five give eleven.
<bookmark mark='test'/>But adding the inputs and four also gives eleven for two and five.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>For four and one, our rule gives thirteen, but adding and four gives nine.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>One pair fits many rules, so we show four pairs.
